title: [Security follow-up] Remove temporary http-cache-semantics audit exception when upstream fixes CVE-2026-93748
body:
ROADMAP_ID=SECURITY_FOLLOWUP_HTTP_CACHE_SEMANTICS
PROPOSED_PHASE=FOLLOW_UP / DEPENDENCY_SECURITY

## Context
On 2026-10-03, the P2 exact-head CI began failing `pnpm audit --audit-level moderate` because the registry newly reports CVE-2026-93748 / GHSA-ch52-4w7c-c8xp against `http-cache-semantics <=4.2.0`.

Upstream status at triage time:
- npm latest is still `http-cache-semantics@4.2.0`.
- No patched release exists.
- upstream issue kornelski/http-cache-semantics#56 remains open.
- upstream proposed fix PR #58 remains open/unreviewed.

## KIRARI reachability assessment
- KIRARI receives the package transitively only through `astro@7.3.5`.
- Astro's source usage is in `packages/astro/src/assets/build/remote.ts` for remote-image build cache TTL calculation.
- That code calls `CachePolicy.storable()` and `timeToLive()`; it does not call the vulnerable `satisfiesWithoutRevalidation()` / `_varyMatches()` reuse path described by the advisory.
- KIRARI's Site output is static and the delivered composition artifact contains `dist` + provenance, not Node dependencies.

## Temporary policy
P2 may carry a narrowly-scoped pnpm 9 `auditConfig.ignoreCves` entry for **CVE-2026-93748 only**. The CI command remains `pnpm audit --audit-level moderate`; all other moderate/high/critical advisories continue to fail the gate.

This is not acceptance of arbitrary unfixable advisories and must not be expanded without separate evidence.

## Exit criteria
- A maintainer-published fixed `http-cache-semantics` release (or an official Astro dependency change) is available.
- Upgrade the resolved dependency through the supported upstream path.
- Remove the CVE-2026-93748 audit exception.
- `pnpm audit --audit-level moderate` passes without the exception.
- Existing Site/composition/security CI remains green.

No production deployment or P3 work is part of this issue.
